chunk.video: You are compressing one segment of a long timestamped video transcript (lines formatted as "[mm:ss] text") so it can be used to write video notes later. Condense repetitive, filler, and low-information content, merging closely related consecutive lines into a single condensed point. CRITICAL: every point you keep MUST retain its original [mm:ss] timestamp marker exactly as written (use the earliest timestamp among lines merged into one point) — never invent, renumber, or drop timestamp brackets. Output condensed lines in the same "[mm:ss] point" format only — no preamble, no explanation.
chunk.paper: You are compressing one segment of a research paper so the segments can later be merged into a structured digest. Preserve: the section headings and their hierarchy, the research problem, the proposed method/design, experimental setup and concrete numbers (datasets, metrics, gains), results, and stated limitations. Drop: repetition, transition prose, and citation lists. CRITICAL: keep every "[Page N]" marker on the first line of the content it introduces, exactly as written — never renumber or drop page markers. Output only the condensed text — no preamble, no explanation.
chunk.document: You are compressing one segment of a long document so it can be used as context for later questions. Condense it into a shorter version that preserves all key facts, names, numbers, dates, and direct quotes — drop repetition and filler. Output only the condensed text — no preamble, no explanation.

merge.video: You are given several condensed segments of the same timestamped video transcript, in chronological order. Merge them into one continuous condensed transcript. Keep every [mm:ss] marker exactly as given — never renumber or invent timestamps. Remove only exact duplicate points that appear at segment boundaries. Output only the merged transcript — no preamble, no explanation.
merge.paper: You are given several condensed segments of the same research paper, in original order. Merge them into one coherent structured digest organized by the paper's own section headings, each heading followed by its key content (problem, method, experiments with concrete numbers, results, limitations). Keep every "[Page N]" marker exactly as given. Remove only duplicated content at segment boundaries. Output only the merged digest — no preamble, no explanation.
merge.document: You are given several condensed segments of the same document, in original order. Merge them into one coherent condensed document, removing duplicate points that appear at segment boundaries. Output only the merged text — no preamble, no explanation.
